body.statement:
Adopt the convention \(\operatorname{Bell}(0)=1\).  For a fixed factual cell \(v\), an \(h\)-element normalized context set \(\mathcal H\), and a layer \(i\), define
\[
A_i(v)=\left\{w\in\mathcal H:
w(t)=v_t\text{ for every }t\leq i\text{ with }t\in\operatorname{dom}(w)\right\}.
\]
The set \(A_i(v)\) is the block of the complete-prefix partition \(\pi_i\) containing the factual context for every feasible prefix in that cell.  Consequently the computable restriction
\[
\pi_i\big|_{\mathcal H\setminus A_i(v)}
\]
is an exact uniform continuation state for terminal predecessor-only normalized conjunctions \(\gamma^{\circ}\), and it takes at most \(\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)\) values.  This bound is attained in the residual sense: for every \(h\geq1\), one explicitly listed binary instance on the complete-predecessor carrier \(\mathfrak F\), with one fixed factual cell and one fixed \(h\)-context system, has \(\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)\) reachable prefixes that are pairwise distinguishable by common legal one-coordinate suffixes and terminal normalized conjunctions.  Hence
\[
\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h-1).
\]
Replacing the partition-state count in \(\mathsf C_1\) gives the improved runtime
\[
\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
\]
This equality is a worst-case exact-state count and does not assert an \(h\log h\) or any other running-time lower bound.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a factual cell \(v\), a layer \(i\), and a feasible response system \(f\in F_v\).  By Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}factual\text{-}fibre}\),
\[
E(f,\varnothing)_{\leq i}=v_{\leq i}. \tag{1}
\]
We first identify the factual block.  Recall
\[
A_i(v)=\left\{w\in\mathcal H:
w(t)=v_t\text{ for every }t\leq i\text{ with }t\in\operatorname{dom}(w)\right\}. \tag{2}
\]
The factual context \(\varnothing\) belongs to \(A_i(v)\), so this set is nonempty.

Let \(w\in A_i(v)\).  We prove by induction on \(t\leq i\) that
\[
E(f,w)_{\leq t}=v_{\leq t}. \tag{3}
\]
The assertion before the first coordinate is vacuous.  Suppose it holds through \(t-1\).  If \(t\in\operatorname{dom}(w)\), equations (2) and the intervention clause of ordered evaluation give
\[
E(f,w)_t=w(t)=v_t. \tag{4}
\]
If \(t\notin\operatorname{dom}(w)\), the induction hypothesis and the natural clause of ordered evaluation give
\[
E(f,w)_t
=f_t(E(f,w)_{<t})
=f_t(v_{<t})
=E(f,\varnothing)_t
=v_t, \tag{5}
\]
where the last equality is (1).  This proves (3).

Conversely, let \(w\notin A_i(v)\), and choose the least \(t\leq i\) such that \(t\in\operatorname{dom}(w)\) and \(w(t)\neq v_t\).  At that coordinate, ordered evaluation and (1) yield
\[
E(f,w)_t=w(t)\neq v_t=E(f,\varnothing)_t. \tag{6}
\]
Thus \(w\) does not have the factual complete prefix.  Equations (3) and (6), together with Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}prefix\text{-}partition}\), prove that \(A_i(v)\) is exactly the block of \(\pi_i\) containing \(\varnothing\).  In particular, this entire block is computable from \(v\), \(\mathcal H\), and \(i\), independently of all selected response rows.

Put \(K_i(v)=\mathcal H\setminus A_i(v)\).  Because \(A_i(v)\) is one whole block, \(\pi_i\) is reconstructed uniquely from its restriction to \(K_i(v)\) by adjoining the known block \(A_i(v)\):
\[
\pi_i=\left\{A_i(v)\right\}\cup
\left(\pi_i\big|_{K_i(v)}\right). \tag{7}
\]
Therefore two feasible prefixes with the same restricted partition in (7) have the same full partition.  The partition-continuation theorem then gives exactly the same support of all later world-value columns under every later factual and normalized-query pin.  Hence those prefixes give the same acceptance answer for every common legal suffix and every terminal normalized conjunction, so the restriction in (7) is exact under Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}residual\text{-}minimality\text{-}handle}\).

Since \(A_i(v)\) contains the factual context,
\[
|K_i(v)|\leq h-1. \tag{8}
\]
There are \(\operatorname{Bell}(|K_i(v)|)\) partitions of this labelled complement.  Moreover, if \(q\leq h-1\), adjoining each of \(h-1-q\) new labels as a singleton injects the partitions of a \(q\)-element set into those of an \((h-1)\)-element set.  Thus
\[
\operatorname{Bell}(|K_i(v)|)\leq\operatorname{Bell}(h-1), \tag{9}
\]
and (7)--(9) prove
\[
\rho(h)\leq\operatorname{Bell}(h-1). \tag{10}
\]
The transition proof used by the single-conjunction compiler depends on the current full partition, which (7) reconstructs without search.  Substituting (9) for its former \(B_h\) state count and leaving its representative-column bound unchanged gives
\[
\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}). \tag{11}
\]
The input still explicitly supplies the alphabets and raw conjunction, so the normalization and input-reading charges already present in the single-conjunction compiler theorem remain inside the polynomial factor.

We now prove the matching residual lower bound on one fixed cell.  Put
\[
m=h-1,
\qquad
J=\{1,\ldots,m\}. \tag{12}
\]
Use binary variables in the order
\[
S\prec (Z_C)_{\varnothing\neq C\subsetneq J}\prec Y, \tag{13}
\]
with any fixed order among the selector variables \(Z_C\).  When \(m\leq1\), the selector family is empty.  Every alphabet is the explicitly listed nonempty finite set \(\{0,1\}\), satisfying Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}alphabets}\).  Fix the factual cell \(v\) to be zero at every coordinate.

For each \(j\in J\), define an intervention context \(I_j\) by
\[
\operatorname{dom}(I_j)=\{S\}\cup
\{Z_C:\varnothing\neq C\subsetneq J,\ j\in C\},
\qquad
I_j(t)=1\quad(t\in\operatorname{dom}(I_j)). \tag{14}
\]
No \(I_j\) intervenes on \(Y\).  The context set is
\[
\mathcal H=\{\varnothing\}\cup\{I_j:j\in J\}. \tag{15}
\]
It has size \(h\): each nonfactual context intervenes on \(S\), and when \(m\geq2\), the singleton selector \(Z_{\{j\}}\) distinguishes \(I_j\) from every \(I_{j'}\) with \(j'\neq j\); when \(m=1\), there is only one nonfactual context.  Assign the factual row of \(S\) the value zero.  Then the factual world starts with value zero, while all worlds \(I_j\) start with their intervention value one.  Hence after \(S\) the factual context is a singleton block and all nonfactual contexts form one block.

Let \(\tau\in\operatorname{Part}(J)\) be arbitrary.  We prescribe complete-predecessor response rows through the selector coordinates.  At each \(Z_C\), give the factual predecessor tuple output zero.  For every predecessor tuple reached by a context \(I_j\) that is natural at \(Z_C\), prescribe
\[
f^{\tau}_{Z_C}(x_{<Z_C})=
\begin{cases}
0,&C\text{ is a block of }\tau,\\
1,&C\text{ is not a block of }\tau.
\end{cases} \tag{16}
\]
This prescription is consistent.  Factual and nonfactual predecessor tuples differ already at \(S\).  Within the nonfactual worlds, contexts with the same predecessor tuple receive the same prescribed value in (16), while intervened contexts do not call the response function at that coordinate.  Distinct predecessor tuples are independent arguments of a complete-predecessor function.  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}complete\text{-}predecessor\text{-}functions}\) therefore permits the prescribed rows, and assigning zero on all unencountered tuples completes each response table.

If \(C\) is not a block of \(\tau\), every nonfactual world appends one at \(Z_C\): a world with \(j\in C\) receives intervention value one by (14), and every other world is natural and receives one by (16).  Thus this coordinate causes no split among nonfactual worlds.  If \(C\) is a block of \(\tau\), the worlds indexed by \(C\) append one and all other nonfactual worlds append zero, so this coordinate separates \(C\) from its complement inside every current block.  Complete-prefix blocks can split but cannot merge.  Since every block of \(\tau\) other than a possible block \(J\) is a nonempty proper subset and hence has a selector in (13), it follows that after all selectors the partition is exactly
\[
P_{\tau}=\bigl\{\{\varnothing\}\bigr\}\cup\tau. \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, indices in the same \(\tau\)-block append the same value at every selector, while indices in different blocks are separated at the selector indexed by either one of those blocks that is a proper subset of \(J\).  The factual path remains zero throughout by construction, so all \(P_{\tau}\) are reachable in the same factual cell \(v\).  Thus (17) supplies \(\operatorname{Bell}(m)\) feasible prefixes.

We show that these prefixes are pairwise residual-distinct.  Take \(\tau\neq\sigma\).  Since partitions are equivalence relations, there exist \(a,b\in J\) that are in different blocks of one partition and in the same block of the other.  Call the former partition \(\alpha\) and the latter \(\beta\).  Define
\[
q(j)=\mathbf 1\{j\text{ is in the }\alpha\text{-block containing }b\}. \tag{18}
\]
Then \(q\) is constant on every \(\alpha\)-block, but
\[
q(a)=0,
\qquad
q(b)=1, \tag{19}
\]
even though \(a\) and \(b\) lie in the same \(\beta\)-block.

Use the terminal conjunction
\[
\gamma_q^{\circ}
=\{Y_{\varnothing}=0\}\wedge
\bigwedge_{j\in J}\{Y_{I_j}=q(j)\}. \tag{20}
\]
It is explicit and unnested.  Every intervention in (20) concerns only predecessors of \(Y\), and no context intervenes on \(Y\); Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}query\text{-}normalizer}\) therefore leaves (20) unchanged.  All contexts in (15) occur, so its normalized context set is exactly \(\mathcal H\).

After the prefix \(P_{\alpha}\), distinct blocks have distinct complete predecessor tuples by (17), and the required value in (20) is constant on each block by (18); the factual singleton requires zero.  Define one terminal complete-predecessor table by assigning the required value to each of these finitely many reached tuples and zero to every unlisted tuple.  This is a legal suffix and makes (20) true after \(P_{\alpha}\).  Use the same terminal table after \(P_{\beta}\).  The contexts \(I_a\) and \(I_b\) have the same complete prefix by (17), are both natural at \(Y\) by (14), and hence call the same terminal response row.  Ordered evaluation forces
\[
E(f,I_a)_Y=E(f,I_b)_Y, \tag{21}
\]
whereas (19)--(20) require the two values to be zero and one.  Thus (20) is false after \(P_{\beta}\).  This common legal suffix and terminal normalized conjunction distinguish the two prefixes.

Every pair among the \(\operatorname{Bell}(m)\) prefixes in (17) is therefore residual-distinct.  For \(m=0\), there is one prefix and the same lower bound is vacuous but valid.  Hence
\[
\rho(h)\geq\operatorname{Bell}(m)=\operatorname{Bell}(h-1). \tag{22}
\]
Combining (10) and (22) proves the claimed equality and the runtime (11).  The construction counts exact continuation states; it supplies no lower bound on the time required to encode or manipulate a state and therefore no \(h\log h\) time lower bound.
body.justification: The fixed factual cell determines one entire partition block, while every partition of the remaining contexts is jointly realizable and residual-distinct in a binary worst-case instance.
body.gap: This resolves the coarsest uniform causal continuation count and improves the compiler's Bell-number factor without turning a state lower bound into a time lower bound.
body.consumer: The single-conjunction compiler can use the exact one-smaller-context Bell number as its partition-state factor.
